sanskrit: अकीर्तिं चापि भूतानि कथयिष्यन्ति तेऽव्ययाम् । संभावितस्य चाकीर्तिर्मरणादतिरिच्यते ॥
hindiTranslation: और सब प्राणी भी तेरी सदा रहनेवाली अपकीर्तिका कथन अर्थात निंदा करेंगे ।  वह अपकीर्ति सम्मानित मनुष्यके लिये मृत्युसे भी बढ़कर दुःखदायी होती है ॥
englishTranslation: And all beings will speak of your everlasting disgrace. For an honored person, disgrace is worse than death.
essence: A honored life can be wounded more by shame than by death.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: People will keep speaking of your disgrace, and for someone who has been honored, that shame feels worse than death.
simpleInsight: Honor can feel more fragile than life itself, and avoiding your duty can wound it deeply.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna has lowered his bow and is wavering. Krishna warns him that if he turns away now, the world will remember his disgrace instead of his greatness. For a warrior known for honor, that loss cuts deeper than death.
modernRelevance: In a small town, the man who ran from a fight to save himself may be talked about for decades. Krishna tells Arjuna that for someone honoured, that kind of lasting disgrace is worse than death.
translationLiteral: अकीर्तिम् (disgrace) / च (and) / अपि (also) / भूतानि (beings) / कथयिष्यन्ति (will speak) / ते (of you) / अव्ययाम् (everlasting) / संभावितस्य (of one who has been honored) / च (and) / अकीर्तिः (disgrace) / मरणात् (than death) / अतिरिच्यते (is greater)
insight: Krishna warns that people will speak of Arjuna's disgrace for ever, and for the honoured that is worse than death.
